item.title: Users & login
item.description:
Stella runs in one of two modes, controlled by auth.enabled.

Single user

auth.enabled: false (the default). There is no login, and all data belongs to one built-in local account. The /mcp endpoint (when enabled) has no auth either, so put it behind a trusted network (Tailscale, localhost, VPN) if you expose it.

item.title: Cards
item.description:
Data model

  • Group: an optional folder for decks. A deck belongs to at most one group.
  • Deck: a named collection of facts (name up to 32 characters, description, optional cover image, optional group).
  • Tag: a free label; a deck can carry any number of them, independent of groups.
  • Fact: the content itself, a front and a back, plus an optional image and audio file per side. A fact belongs to one deck.
  • Card: one direction of quizzing derived from a fact. The forward card (front → back) always exists; the reverse card (back → front) is optional and needs a non-empty back.

Groups are one per deck (exclusive categories); tags are many per deck (cross-cutting labels).

item.title: Reviewing
item.description: Stella schedules cards with a Go port of Mnemosyne’s SM2 algorithm. After each card you grade how well you remembered it, from 0 (blackout) to 5 (perfect recall), and the grade sets when you see the card next: well-remembered cards come back at ever longer intervals, forgotten ones come back soon.

item.title: Import & export
item.description: Decks and groups can be exported and imported as archives. An export carries the content, the media, and each card’s scheduling state and review history, so an imported deck resumes where it left off.

item.title: MCP server
item.description: Stella can expose a Model Context Protocol server, so an AI assistant can create decks and cards for you, tag and group them, and edit or move existing cards.

item.title: Device sync
item.description: stella-x4 is a standalone spaced-repetition firmware for the Xteink X4 e-ink reader. It runs the same SM2 review loop offline, from the SD card, and syncs with a Stella server over WiFi.
